text: Thomas Richard Suozzi, born August 31, 1962, in Glen Cove, New York, is an American politician serving as the U.S. representative for New York's 3rd congressional district since 2024 and previously from 2017 to 2023. A member of the Democratic Party, he served as county executive of Nassau County from 2002 to 2009 and was mayor of Glen Cove for eight years, including four terms beginning in 1993. His district, which is largely suburban, includes northern Nassau County and parts of northeastern Queens. Suozzi ran unsuccessfully against Eliot Spitzer for the Democratic nomination for governor of New York in 2006. He was elected to the U.S. House of Representatives in 2016 and reelected in 2018 and 2020. He retired from Congress in 2022 to run for the Democratic gubernatorial nomination, losing to incumbent governor Kathy Hochul. In October 2023, Suozzi announced he would run for his congressional seat in 2024. After George Santos was expelled from Congress in December 2023, a special election was scheduled for February 13, 2024; Suozzi was selected as the Democratic nominee and won the election by a margin of 54% to 46%, reclaiming the seat for Democrats. He served out the remainder of Santos's term, which expired in January 2025. Suozzi graduated from Chaminade High School in 1980 and earned a Bachelor of Science in accounting from Boston College in 1984. He worked as a certified public accountant for two years before earning a Juris Doctor from Fordham University School of Law in 1989. He began his career at Arthur Andersen, served as a law clerk for Thomas Collier Platt Jr. of the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York, and worked as a commercial litigator at Shearman & Sterling until 1993. After public office, he worked as an attorney of counsel at Harris Beach and as a consultant for Cablevision and Lazard until 2016, and joined Actum as a co-chair in 2023. His father, Joseph A. Suozzi, was an attorney and served as mayor of Glen Cove from 1956 to 1960; Joseph was originally from Ruvo del Monte, Italy. Suozzi's mother, Marguerite (née Holmes), was of Irish and English descent and worked as an operating room nurse at Glen Cove Hospital. As mayor, Suozzi focused on environmental cleanup and redevelopment of brownfield and superfund sites, including the permanent closure and dismantling of the Glen Cove incinerator in 1994 and the demolition and redevelopment of the Li Tungsten Refinery grounds in 1998. He was elected Nassau County executive in 2001, becoming the first Democrat elected to the position in 30 years amid a fiscal crisis marked by a $300 million annual deficit, billions in debt, and a credit rating one level above junk. He cut spending, reduced borrowing, oversaw 11 county bond upgrades, eliminated deficits, and accumulated surpluses, earning praise from independent institutions and being named a Public Official of the Year by Governing Magazine in 2005. He also implemented a "no wrong door" program to centralize access to social services. Suozzi narrowly lost the 2009 county executive election to Ed Mangano and ran again in 2013, losing by a margin of 59% to 41%. In 2006, he declared his candidacy for governor, receiving support from figures like Victor Rodriguez and financiers including Kenneth Langone, Richard Grasso, and David Mack, and received a standing ovation at a speech before the New York State Conference of Mayors; he ultimately lost the primary to Spitzer with 18% of the vote to Spitzer's 82%. In 2021, Suozzi announced his candidacy for governor in the 2022 election, opposing a proposal by Kathy Hochul to allow accessory dwelling units on single-family lots, stating he supported efforts to address housing shortages but opposed ending single-family housing. He placed third in the Democratic primary with 12% of the vote. In June 2016, Suozzi won a five-way Democratic primary in the 3rd district, defeating Republican Jack Martins in the general election with 53% to 47%, beginning his service in the 115th Congress in January 2017. In June 2018, he won the Democratic primary unopposed and defeated Dan DeBono in the general election with 59% to 41%. In June 2020, he won a three-way Democratic primary with 66.5% of the vote and defeated George Santos in the general election with 56% to 43%. In November 2023, Suozzi announced his candidacy for the 3rd district, and after Santos's expulsion, he declared his candidacy for the special election. He was selected as the Democratic nominee on December 7, 2023, and defeated Republican Mazi Melesa Pilip, a Nassau County Legislature member, in the February 13, 2024, special election. Suozzi and Pilip both campaigned on the issue of migrant influx and were described as staunch supporters of Israel. In Congress, Suozzi prioritized tax policy and authored legislation to restore the state and local tax (SALT) deduction, which was capped at $10,000 in 2017; he led efforts to eliminate the cap, though the initiative failed. In 2021, the Campaign Legal Center filed an ethics complaint alleging he failed to report nearly 300 stock transactions worth between $3.2 million and $11 million, but the House Ethics Committee ruled in July 2022 that the violations were not "knowing or willful" and dismissed the case. Suozzi voted in favor of military aid packages for Ukraine, Israel, and Taiwan in 2024. After Kamala Harris's 2024 presidential defeat, he criticized the Democratic Party's stance on transgender participation in girls' sports and what he described as a "general attack on traditional values," drawing political backlash. On January 1, 2025, he wrote an op-ed in The New York Times calling for Democrats to work with the incoming Trump administration and advocate for political compromise on parts of Trump's agenda. In January 2025, he was elected Democratic co-chair of the Problem Solvers Caucus and joined 46 House Democrats in voting for the Laken Riley Act. On March 6, 2025, he was one of ten Democrats who voted with all Republicans to censure Al Green for interrupting President Donald Trump's State of the Union Address. He opposed a potential New York redistricting effort in response to Trump's push for Republican-led district drawing in Texas for the 2026 midterms. Suozzi married his wife Helene (née Wrotniak) in 1993; they live in Glen Cove and have three children. His son Joe is a minor league baseball player who has played in the New York Mets organization. Suozzi is Catholic.
